newsitem.title: CROATIA: Demand pushes Croatian lending rate up to 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Demand pushes Croatian lending rate up to 11 pct.

text.p: Stronger demand by borrowers for term loans pushed the Croatian average lending rate up to 11 percent on Wednesday from 10.1 percent.
Dealers put total trade at 22.1 million kuna, of which 18 million were fresh borrowings, against 50 million on offer.
The rates were unchanged at 9.0 percent for call money and insurers' one-week funds.
One-month loans were made at between 12 and 15 percent.
Overnight settlements totalled 20 million kuna on Tuesday as one bank borrowed money to maintain its mandatory reserve.
The central bank's kuna midrate firmed to 5.5524 against the dollar but was little changed at 3.5613 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
